subject: art-design
title: Public vs Private Art
welcome_lead: Who is art for? Plinths, commissions, and contested monuments.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: public art, private collections, and contested space.
final_note: Art in public space is never neutral.

walkthroughs.body_html: Public art ranges from monumental sculpture (Antony Gormley's Angel of the North, 1998) to participatory practice (Jeremy Deller). State and corporate funding bring questions of accountability and intention.

Trafalgar Square's empty Fourth Plinth has, since 1998, hosted rotating contemporary commissions — Rachel Whiteread, Marc Quinn, Yinka Shonibare — turning a colonial space into a forum for living artists.
In June 2020, the Edward Colston statue (slave trader, erected 1895) was toppled in Bristol during BLM protests. The debate about contested monuments has become a central A-Level critical theme.
